title: Fake News in Sheep’s Clothing: Robust Fake News Detection Against LLM-Empowered Style Attacks

problem.claim: LLM-powered style mimicry can make fake news resemble trustworthy sources and undermine text-based fake news detectors.

gap.claim: Existing detectors are vulnerable to stylistic variations because style-related features can be exploited in attacks.

contributions.claim: SheepDog is a style-robust fake news detector that prioritizes content over style when determining veracity.
The approach uses LLM-generated style-diverse reframings, style-agnostic training for consistent predictions, and content-focused veracity attributions.
Content-focused veracity attributions distill content-centric debunking guidelines from LLMs as supplementary cues for veracity prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: LLM-camouflaged fake news reduced the F1 score of state-of-the-art text-based detectors by up to 38%.
Extensive experiments on three real-world benchmarks demonstrated SheepDog's style robustness and adaptability across various backbones.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fake and real news are commonly perceived as having distinct writing styles.
Style features can be exploited by malicious actors using LLMs to mimic trustworthy news sources.
LLM-camouflaged fake news substantially undermines existing text-based detectors.
SheepDog addresses the vulnerability by emphasizing content over style through reframing, style-agnostic training, and content-focused attributions.
The authors report experiments on three real-world benchmarks covering style robustness and backbone adaptability.

unknowns: Benchmark identities and dataset sizes are not specified.
The abstract does not report comparative performance values for SheepDog beyond the stated detector degradation.
Training, reframing, attribution, and backbone implementation details are omitted.
